hypothesis: A correctly mapped six-hour ASOS maximum wholly inside the NWS local-standard climate day, conservatively reduced by2F, may provide a reliable lower bound on the final reported daily high. This is a data-qualification hypothesis, not a profitable trading claim.

observations.source: Iowa Environmental Mesonet raw routine/SPECI METAR archive, original raw text retained
reject: conflicting raw reports at same station/valid timestamp
observations.six_hour_group: exactly one standalone1snTTT afterRMK; signedtenthsC, nearestwholeF must be within0.100001F
observations.synoptic_window: Raw report must be within15minutes of nominal00/06/12/18UTC; entire nominal-6h-15m through nominal+15m interval must be inside climate day
observations.assumed_availability: nominal report end plus60minutes, unverified historical dissemination, never use valid timestamp as actual receipt

decision.selection: First fixed decision time with any provably resolved listed binary contract using available lower bound; closest crossed integer outcome boundary, then ticker/side tie order; one candidate/city-day; no prices or outcomes supplied to selection
decision.metadata: Strict binary strike_type machine bounds, exact yes_sub_title integer interval must agree; correct station rules/open/close required; incomplete ladders do not reject individually resolvable contracts

evaluation.numeric_final: Finite whole-F expiration_value and settlement_value_dollars agree with official YES/NO label; missing stays unverified
evaluation.primary: Whether recovered lower bound exceeds final high; every such contradiction is retained and rejects locked-bound interpretation
evaluation.secondary: Selected logical YES/NO outcome label/numeric agreement; no PnL, quote, order or fill inference

automatic_rejection: Any independently numerically verified bound contradiction rejects mechanism version; never increase buffer or remove losing cases after inspection. Missing/partial station/rule/settlement data is visible and blocks data-qualification success.
